newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end flat, EVN knocked lower.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end flat, EVN knocked lower.

text.p: Austrian shares ended flat on Tuesday, with losses in regional utility EVN offset by gains in oil and chemicals group OMV, and traders said the ATX index remained locked in its 1,060 to 1,080 points range.
The ATX of 21 blue-chip shares closed 0.19 points down at 1,072.90. Eight issues closed up, 12 down and one unchanged.
EVN was by far the day's biggest decliner after the company disappointed investors with a flat 1995/6 net profit despite a 24 percent jump in pre-tax earnings, which reached a record.
Its shares closed 3.88 percent down at 1,487 schillings, reversing a month of steady gains in an otherwise stagnant Vienna market.
"The market was obviously expecting more. The firm had flagged 1995/6 would be a very good year so the flat net profit was a bit of a surprise," said a trader.

OMV was the session's biggest gainer, piling on 2.65 percent to 1,085 schillings in what brokers described as a technical break-out. OMV also announced new oil and gas finds north of Vienna shortly before the market closed.
High grade steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm was under selling pressure ahead of the firm's quarterly results next week. "People aren't expecting a good set of figures," said a dealer.
November ATX futures stood 2.5 points higher at 1,075.5. The broad-based Vienna bourse index was 0.03 points down at 412.11 -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
